title: Add profiles to your traced Kubernetes services

blocks.content:
Your traces show which request is slow. Profiles show what code made it slow.

**Before you begin.** This guide is only for Kubernetes services that you onboarded with Instrumentation Hub. For anything else, refer to [Configure the client to send profiles](https://grafana.com/docs/pyroscope/latest/configure-client/).
First, turn on profiling for the namespace that runs your traced service.

blocks.reftarget: button[aria-label^='Configure pipeline settings for all instrumented services in namespace']
blocks.content: Select your cluster, then click the settings icon next to the namespace that runs your traced service. The icon appears only for namespaces with instrumented services.
Click **Apply**. The setting applies to every instrumented service in the namespace.
Profiling is on for that namespace, with no code changes.

Now check that profiles arrive. If Profiles Drilldown still shows its welcome page after a few minutes, restart the Alloy daemonset on your cluster, then refresh your browser. Replace `<NAMESPACE>` with the namespace where you installed Alloy:

```bash
kubectl rollout restart daemonset -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy-daemonset -n <NAMESPACE>
```
Find your service. If you still see the welcome page, restart the Alloy daemonset as described above, then refresh your browser.
Click **Flame graph** to see where a service spends its time.
Profiles are flowing next to your traces.
